summary: Rabbi Harari explores the concept of the Bet HaMikdash not merely as a destination for ritual, but as a continuous journey of searching for a relationship with Hashem. He draws parallels between the travels of Avraham Abinu and the journey of Bnei Yisrael in the midbar, arguing that the destruction of the Bet HaMikdash occurred because the people treated their connection to Hashem as a mechanical routine rather than an ongoing search. The class concludes by framing the exile as an opportunity to return to a life of seeking Hashem, similar to the life of Avraham Abinu.
questions: Why was the Bet HaMikdash considered a journey?
How does the life of Avraham Abinu relate to the travels of Bnei Yisrael in the midbar?
Why do we commemorate the destruction of the Bet HaMikdash on the 9th of Av instead of the 10th?
What does it mean to treat a relationship with Hashem as a journey rather than a destination?
How does the prophecy of Yeshayahu explain the downfall of the Bet HaMikdash?
